q: בת 78, סובלת מסוכרת לא מאוזנת, ירידה בשמיעה, ופרפור עליות. היא מתגוררת בביתה לבדה, ולאחרונה אובחנה כסובלת מדמנציה. לאחרונה אירעו מספר אירועים: השכנים מצאו אותה משוטטת ברחוב ולא מוצאת את ביתה, הוזמן מכבי אש עקב שריפה שפרצה בדירה מסיר שנשאר על האש. בביקור בית של הרווחה מתברר שלא התרחצה ולא החליפה בגדים זמן ממושך ואכלה מזון מקולקל. הוחלט להעביר אותה למסגרת מוסדית. מה הסטטוס התפקודי של אישה זו?
o: המטופלת עם ירידה קוגניטיבית, הגורמת לה לפגיעה משמעותית בתפקוד היומיומי ולכן תוגדר כתשושת נפש
המטופלת מתהלכת בעצמה וזקוקה רק לעזרה ב- IADL ולכן תוגדר כתשושה
המטופלת זקוקה להשגחה צמודה ואינה יכולה להתרחץ בעצמה ולכן תוגדר כסיעודית
סוג המסגרת המתאימה תלוי בערך המספרי של מבחן MMSE
explanation:
המטופלת מציגה פגיעה קוגניטיבית עם סכנה לבטיחותה וצורך בהשגחה. ההגדרה המתאימה במפתח היא **תשושת נפש**; ההגדרות בנוהל מבדילות בין עזרה חלקית, מצב סיעודי וצורך בהכוונה ובהשגחה בשל פגיעה קוגניטיבית (נוהל 0.2.1, עמ׳ 2).

**א. המטופלת עם ירידה קוגניטיבית, הגורמת לה לפגיעה משמעותית בתפקוד היומיומי ולכן תוגדר כתשושת נפש.** נכונה, זו האפשרות הרשמית, והיא מתאימה לדגש בהגדרת תשושת נפש על פגיעה בזיכרון ובהתמצאות, הכוונה בניידות והשגחה על הבטיחות. השיטוט והסכנות הביתיות בשאלה מדגימים צורך זה (עמ׳ 2).
**ב. המטופלת מתהלכת בעצמה וזקוקה רק לעזרה ב- IADL ולכן תוגדר כתשושה.** שגויה, הגדרת תשוש מתייחסת לעזרה חלקית בפעולות היומיום. התיאור כולל גם קושי ברחצה ובלבוש וסיכון המחייב השגחה, ולכן אינו מצטמצם לעזרה בפעולות מורכבות (עמ׳ 2).
**ג. המטופלת זקוקה להשגחה צמודה ואינה יכולה להתרחץ בעצמה ולכן תוגדר כסיעודית.** שגויה, השגחה וקושי ברחצה לבדם אינם ממלאים את צירוף התנאים להגדרה סיעודית: נדרש גם אחד המצבים המנויים בנוהל, כגון ריתוק, אי שליטה בסוגרים או הליכה בקושי רב. אלה לא תוארו בשאלה (עמ׳ 2).
**ד. סוג המסגרת המתאימה תלוי בערך המספרי של מבחן MMSE.** שגויה, הנוהל מגדיר את המסגרת לפי מצב ותפקוד בפועל, לרבות צורך בהכוונה ובהשגחה. ציון יחיד במבחן קוגניטיבי אינו מחליף את התנאים התפקודיים (עמ׳ 2).

**נקודת המפתח:** ההגדרות אינן חלוקה מוחלטת בין קוגניטיבי לגופני; יש לבדוק את מכלול התנאים בנוהל 0.2.1, עמ׳ 2.

מקור: משרד הבריאות, הגדרת מושגים, נוהל 0.2.1, עמ׳ 2.
ref: משרד הבריאות: בחירת מוסד האשפוז המתאים לקשיש

q: מה מתאר את הטיפול במחלת אלצהיימר עם מעכבי כולין אסטרז?
o: מרבית החולים חווים עצירה או האטה של הירידה הקוגניטיבית
מחקרים חדשים מראים שסוג זה של תרופות אינו Cost-Effective
מעכבים מעבר מ- MCI למחלת אלצהיימר
קיימים במתן פומי בלבד
explanation:
Official answer: most patients experience arrest or slowing of cognitive decline. The claim that these drugs delay progression from MCI to Alzheimer disease is wrong under the official key and is not supported by Hazzard (p. 911).

**Acetylcholinesterase inhibitors** (donepezil, rivastigmine, and galantamine) increase acetylcholine availability at neuronal synapses. Their cognitive benefit is generally modest: stabilization or slower decline, rather than restoration of prior function (pp. 910–911).
"experience a plateau or slowing of their rate of cognitive decline." (p. 911)
"AChEIs have not been shown to be effective in delaying progression from MCI to AD" (p. 911)

**A. Most patients experience arrest or slowing of cognitive decline.** Correct, the source describes a plateau or slower decline in most patients, even without noticeable cognitive improvement (p. 911).
**B. New studies show that these drugs are not cost-effective.** Wrong, newer studies incorporating generic drug prices found these drugs cost-effective; the categorical claim of no cost-effectiveness does not match the source (p. 911).
**C. They delay progression from MCI to Alzheimer disease.** Wrong, this effect has not been demonstrated; these drugs are chiefly recommended for patients who already have a diagnosis of dementia (p. 911).
**D. They are available only orally.** Wrong, rivastigmine also has a transdermal patch, so oral administration is not the only route (p. 912, Table 59-7).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 910–912, Table 59-7.

q: A 69-year-old woman with controlled rheumatoid arthritis takes methotrexate and prednisone 5 mg daily. She develops herpes zoster on her left shoulder and starts oral acyclovir at rash onset. The rash heals, but burning pain in the affected area continues to disrupt sleep more than 90 days after rash onset. Which diagnosis matches this course?
o: Prodromal dermatomal pain preceding the zoster eruption
Postherpetic neuralgia following the zoster eruption
Zoster sine herpete without a cutaneous eruption
Acute neuritis during the initial zoster eruption
explanation:
**Postherpetic neuralgia** is defined by persistent pain at least 90 days after rash onset. Hazzard states, "Postherpetic neuralgia (PHN) is pain 90 or more days after rash onset" and describes burning pain and substantial effects on sleep and daily function (pp. 1725–1726).

**A. Prodromal dermatomal pain preceding the zoster eruption.** Wrong, prodromal symptoms precede the rash; this pain persists long after an established eruption has healed (p. 1726).
**B. Postherpetic neuralgia following the zoster eruption.** Correct, the pain continues beyond the source's temporal definition after a documented zoster eruption (p. 1725).
**C. Zoster sine herpete without a cutaneous eruption.** Wrong, zoster sine herpete is described as dermatomal neuralgia without a skin eruption, whereas this patient had one (p. 1726).
**D. Acute neuritis during the initial zoster eruption.** Wrong, the timing is beyond the acute eruption and meets the PHN definition; acute neuritis does not describe this later course (pp. 1725–1726).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1725, 1726.
ref: Hazzard Ch 107 — OTHER VIRUSES: HUMAN IMMUNODEFICIENCY VIRUS INFECTION AND HERPES ZOSTER
chapterTitle: Other Viruses: Human Immunodeficiency Virus Infection and Herpes Zoster

q: A man with Alzheimer disease taking donepezil reports poor sleep. Which pair of adverse effects is listed for donepezil in Hazzard and should be considered during medication review?
o: Insomnia and bradycardia
Insomnia and tachycardia
Excessive sleep and bradycardia
Excessive sleep and tachycardia
explanation:
**Medication review** should include the adverse effects listed for donepezil. The table includes insomnia and bradycardia or heart block; this supports considering the medication during assessment without establishing that it explains every behavioral symptom (p. 912).
"Bradycardia or heart block, syncope, nausea, diarrhea, insomnia, vomiting, muscle cramps, fatigue, anorexia" (p. 912).

**A. Insomnia and bradycardia.** Correct, both insomnia and bradycardia are listed adverse effects, matching the sleep concern and a recognized cardiac effect (p. 912).
**B. Insomnia and tachycardia.** Wrong, insomnia is listed, but the cardiac effect in the table is bradycardia or heart block rather than tachycardia (p. 912).
**C. Excessive sleep and bradycardia.** Wrong, bradycardia is listed, but the sleep adverse effect in the table is insomnia rather than excessive sleep (p. 912).
**D. Excessive sleep and tachycardia.** Wrong, neither the proposed sleep effect nor the proposed heart-rate direction matches the listed pair (p. 912).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 912.
ref: Hazzard Ch 59 — DEMENTIA INCLUDING ALZHEIMER DISEASE

q: A 76-year-old man with diabetes taking metformin develops a severe acute illness with tissue hypoperfusion around the time of surgery. What is the main reason to avoid metformin in this situation?
o: Concern about frequent hypoglycemia during metformin monotherapy
Concern about lactic acidosis during an illness with hypoperfusion
Concern about increased hepatic glucose production during metformin treatment
Concern about reduced peripheral insulin sensitivity during metformin treatment
explanation:
**Lactic acidosis risk** is the reason to avoid metformin during a major acute illness that reduces tissue perfusion. Hazzard identifies decreased perfusion as a precipitating factor, while describing metformin as a drug that suppresses hepatic glucose production and may improve peripheral insulin sensitivity. (p. 1576)
"Metformin rarely causes hypoglycemia when used alone." (p. 1576)
"during acute hospitalization for any major illness that could result in decreased tissue perfusion as a precipitating factor for lactic acidosis." (p. 1576)

**A. Concern about frequent hypoglycemia during metformin monotherapy.** Wrong, Hazzard states that metformin rarely causes hypoglycemia when used alone; this is not the reason given for avoidance during hypoperfusion. (p. 1576)
**B. Concern about lactic acidosis during an illness with hypoperfusion.** Correct, the acute illness and reduced tissue perfusion match the setting in which Hazzard advises avoiding metformin because of lactic acidosis risk. (p. 1576)
**C. Concern about increased hepatic glucose production during metformin treatment.** Wrong, metformin primarily suppresses hepatic glucose production rather than increasing it. (p. 1576)
**D. Concern about reduced peripheral insulin sensitivity during metformin treatment.** Wrong, metformin may enhance peripheral insulin sensitivity; reduced sensitivity is not the stated reason for avoiding it here. (p. 1576)

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th ed., p. 1576.

q: מהו נזק אפשרי של Tramadol בטיפול בכאב כרוני?
o: מעלה סף לפרכוסים
מעלה סיכון לתמותה
גורם לעצירות בשכיחות גבוהה יותר משאר התרופות האופיואידיות
גורם לדכוי נשימתי בשכיחות גבוהה יותר משאר התרופות האופיואידיות
explanation:
Official answer: ב.

**Increased mortality risk** is listed among tramadol’s harms. The passage does not establish a higher risk than with other opioids or specify a mechanism for the increase (p. 788).

**A. Raises the seizure threshold.** Wrong, the source warns against tramadol in patients with a seizure history; it does not describe a protective effect against seizures (p. 1061).
**B. Increases mortality risk.** Correct, explicitly listed among the drug’s harms, without attribution here to a particular causal mechanism (p. 788).
**C. Causes constipation more often than other opioids.** Wrong, constipation is described as less of a problem with tramadol, which does not support the proposed greater frequency (p. 788).
**D. Causes respiratory depression more often than other opioids.** Wrong, respiratory depression is also described as less of a problem with tramadol; that does not mean the drug is risk-free (p. 788).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 788, 1061.

q: בת 72 עם Rheumatoid Arthritis מטופלת ב- Methotrexate במינון 20 מ"ג פעם בשבוע. היא מעוניינת בקבלת חיסון שפעת. מהי ההמלצה המתאימה ?
o: הפסקה זמנית של Methotrexate לשבועיים
המשך הטיפול ב- Methotrexate ללא שינוי
הורדה זמנית של מינון Methotrexate ל- 10 מ"ג למשך חודש
החלפת הטיפול ל- Leflunomide (Arava)
explanation:
**A. Temporarily stop methotrexate for two weeks.** Correct, this was officially accepted. Hazzard describes possible improvement in vaccine response with a brief methotrexate interruption; the conditions and uncertainty are preserved below (p. 1619).
**B. Continue methotrexate unchanged.** Correct, this was also officially accepted. Acceptance does not mean continuation improves vaccine response; the caveat about disease activity and flare risk is preserved below (p. 1619).
**C. Temporarily reduce methotrexate to 10 mg for one month.** Wrong, the source discusses a brief interruption after vaccination, not this dose-reduction regimen; it is not the regimen supported by the described study (p. 1619).
**D. Switch to leflunomide (Arava).** Wrong, the source does not recommend changing disease-modifying treatment solely for influenza vaccination; the discussion concerns timing of existing treatment around vaccination (p. 1619).

**Official answer: א׳, ב׳** (IMA final official answer key after appeals, September 2024, question 87).

**Hazzard 8e — examination textbook:** Holding methotrexate for two weeks after vaccination may improve response without a significant increase in RA activity in the study described. This does not guarantee freedom from flares in every patient. The question provides no information about disease stability (Hazzard 8e, p. 1619; September 2024 question paper, p. 21).

**Guideline/consensus comparison (secondary source):** The version read, the 2022 ACR guideline, conditionally recommends holding methotrexate for two weeks after influenza vaccination if disease activity permits. Flare risk and shared decision-making matter; the question does not provide enough information to establish that condition (Bass et al., journal p. 453, PDF p. 5; Table 3 on journal p. 454, PDF p. 6).

Source: Hazzard 8e, p. 1619; Bass AR et al. 2022 American College of Rheumatology Guideline for Vaccinations in Patients With Rheumatic and Musculoskeletal Diseases. Arthritis Care Res. 2023;75:449–464. doi:10.1002/acr.25045. https://assets.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltee37abb6b278ab2c/blt1c0ef84075c925cf/vaccinations-guideline-manuscript-2022.pdf.
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Subspecialty official answer key after appeals, Q87

q: כל הנתונים הקליניים הבאים לכאבי גב מהווים RED FLAGS ומצריכים בירור סיסטמי פרט לאחד. מה לא מהווה גורם המחייב בירור סיסטמי?
o: מטופל הסובל מדיכוי חיסוני
ירידה במשקל
שימוש קבוע בסטרואידים
כאב גב מזה שבועיים
explanation:
Table 102-7 lists **red flags for systemic disease** in a patient with back pain. Its duration criterion is more than six weeks; two weeks alone does not meet it (p. 1636).

**A. Immunosuppression.** Wrong, this is not the requested exception: immunosuppression is explicitly listed as a red flag, even when the back pain has been brief (p. 1636).
**B. Weight loss.** Wrong, this is not the exception: unexplained weight loss is listed and warrants investigation of the cause in the context of back pain (p. 1636).
**C. Regular steroid use.** Wrong, this is not the exception: prolonged glucocorticoid use is listed alongside osteoporosis as a reason for further evaluation (p. 1636).
**D. Back pain for two weeks.** Correct, this is the exception. Two weeks alone is not a duration-based red flag; it does not negate other red flags if present (p. 1636).

Source: Hazzard 8e, p. 1636, Table 102-7.

q: בת 74 מדווחת על בריחת שתן לאחר ניתוח החלפת ברך אלקטיבי. מציינת בריחת שתן בדרך לשירותים. איזה מהתערבויות הבאות יכולה להפחית את אירועי בריחת השתן?
o: טיפול תרופתי מקבוצה של Alpha Adrenergic Agonist
תרגול של שלפוחית השתן (Bladder Training)
התאמת סביבה
התערבות כירורגית
explanation:
After knee replacement, impaired mobility can contribute to **functional urinary incontinence** by delaying toilet access. This is a clinical interpretation of the scenario, not proof of a specific postoperative impairment. **Environmental adaptations** directly address difficulty reaching and using a toilet (p. 709, Table 47-9).

**A. An alpha-adrenergic agonist.** Wrong, the table places these agents under stress incontinence; they do not address the functional toilet-access problem targeted by the official answer (p. 709).
**B. Bladder training.** Wrong, training primarily targets urgency with behavioral techniques and requires physical and cognitive capacity and motivation; environmental adaptation directly addresses toilet access here (pp. 709–710).
**C. Environmental adaptation.** Correct, environmental measures are explicitly included in functional-incontinence treatment. Applied to the post-knee-surgery scenario, they facilitate timely toilet access (p. 709; clinical inference).
**D. Surgery.** Wrong, the table assigns surgery to conditions such as obstruction or specific structural problems rather than functional barriers; the scenario provides no basis for such surgery (p. 709).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 709–710.

q: During bladder filling, what immediate relationship between bladder pressure and outlet resistance permits urinary leakage?
o: Bladder pressure remains below outlet resistance as filling proceeds
Bladder pressure stays low while outlet resistance rises during filling
Outlet resistance exceeds bladder pressure despite a detrusor contraction
Bladder pressure exceeds outlet resistance while urine is being stored
explanation:
Urinary continence during filling depends on the **balance of bladder pressure and outlet resistance**. Leakage occurs when bladder pressure exceeds the resistance of the outlet; the source describes both transmitted abdominal pressure in someone with a weak outlet and involuntary bladder contraction as ways this can occur (p. 701).
"If at any time during bladder filling, total bladder pressure exceeds outlet resistance, urinary leakage occurs." (p. 701).
"Transmitted intra-abdominal pressure alone by coughing or sneezing may cause leakage in someone with low outlet resistance pressure or urethral sphincter weakness." (p. 701).

**A. Bladder pressure remains below outlet resistance as filling proceeds.** Wrong, when bladder pressure remains below outlet resistance, the stated pressure condition for leakage is not met (p. 701).
**B. Bladder pressure stays low while outlet resistance rises during filling.** Wrong, low bladder pressure with higher outlet resistance does not supply the pressure relationship needed for leakage (p. 701).
**C. Outlet resistance exceeds bladder pressure despite a detrusor contraction.** Wrong, a contraction can cause leakage, but this option still places outlet resistance above bladder pressure and therefore fails the stated condition (p. 701).
**D. Bladder pressure exceeds outlet resistance while urine is being stored.** Correct, this is the pressure relationship the source states permits leakage during filling (p. 701).

Source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8e (marked), pp. 701.

q: During an Epley maneuver for posterior-canal BPPV, each position is held for approximately 10 to 15 seconds or until vertigo subsides. What is the intended mechanical effect?
o: Move particles from the utricle into the posterior semicircular canal
Move particles from the posterior semicircular canal into the cochlea
Move particles from the horizontal canal into the posterior semicircular canal
Move particles from the posterior semicircular canal into the utricle
explanation:
The **Epley maneuver** uses gravity to reposition loose particles out of the affected posterior canal. Returning them to the utricle removes the source of turbulence and fluctuating endolymphatic pressure described in the chapter (p. 676).
"moves free-floating particles from the posterior semicircular canal into the utricle of the labyrinth by the effects of gravity" (p. 676).

**A. Move particles from the utricle into the posterior semicircular canal.** Wrong, this sends particles into the affected canal, where the chapter places the mechanical disturbance, rather than removing them from it (p. 676).
**B. Move particles from the posterior semicircular canal into the cochlea.** Wrong, the described destination is the utricle, not the cochlea; cochlear transfer is not the repositioning mechanism in this procedure (p. 676).
**C. Move particles from the horizontal canal into the posterior semicircular canal.** Wrong, the treated particles originate in the posterior canal. Moving particles into that canal would not accomplish the evacuation described for this patient (p. 676).
**D. Move particles from the posterior semicircular canal into the utricle.** Correct, gravity moves the offending particles out of the posterior canal into the utricle, resolving the described mechanical disturbance (p. 676).

Source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8e, p. 676.

q: What is the potentially curative treatment for localized pancreatic cancer?
o: Celiac plexus neurolysis
Surgical resection
Biliary stenting
Microencapsulated lipase
explanation:
Surgical resection is the only potentially curative therapy for localized pancreatic cancer and can be safe in carefully selected older adults (p1445).

C. Biliary stenting: Stenting relieves biliary obstruction as palliative care (p1446).
D. Microencapsulated lipase: Lipase supplements address pancreatic insufficiency symptoms (p1446).
A. Celiac plexus neurolysis: Neurolysis is described for pain management (p1446).
